newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing proposes ECB adopt 3-mth repo tenders.
newsitem.headline: Issing proposes ECB adopt 3-mth repo tenders.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing on Thursday recommended that the future European central bank (ECB) supply funds to banks through three-month securities repurchase agreements, or repos, as well as shorter-term repos.

Issing also said there were good reasons to allow banks to use private sector securities as collateral for central bank credit, in addition to government securities, according to the text of a speech.
Gearing the system exclusively to state securities was not to be recommended, Issing said, adding that refinancing methods used so far did not have to be changed.
"One way could be for the ECB, alongside normal repo tenders, to offer a second, longer-term tender model running, say, for three months, with private paper."
That form of refinancing would be especially in the interest of smaller banks, Issing said.
Issing also suggested that the ECB use money supply targeting as well as inflation forecasts as guides to monetary policy.
Adopting a money supply target would help pass on some of the Bundesbank's inflation-fighting credibility to the ECB, Issing said.
But he added that there would be considerable uncertainty in the early stages of monetary union about the empirical basis for money supply targeting.
There would also be uncertainty about financial structures and the transmission process of monetary policy, Issing said.
"A middle road worth thinking about would therefore be to supplement money supply control with an inflation forecast," Issing said.

"During a transition period, until we have sufficient knowledge about actual money demand behaviour in EMU, the advantage of greater flexibility for the central bank should outweigh the disadvantage of a certain loss of public transparency."
The Bundesbank made the text of the speech available in Frankfurt before Issing, who is also the Bundesbank's chief economist, was due to hold at a monetary conference in Luxembourg.
